independent_computation.step_1_what_the_leaf_is: cast_timeline[3]/slot is the ability slot of the 4th cast on the fight's shared cast timeline, in the 'manual_target' fight of scenario syndra_custom_order_60.
independent_computation.step_2_scheduling_law: docs/math-foundations.md §1.1 fixes the scheduling law: 'Ability recasts are scheduled on one shared timeline (the champion has one set of hands): each cast occupies its sourced cast time, an ability recasts when its effective cooldown has elapsed *and* no other cast is in progress, and a cast counts when it *starts* within the window (`_schedule_shared_casts`) ... the shared-timeline version is the superposition with mutual-exclusion, resolved greedily by cast order.' The §5 audit table adds the timed-fight constraint 'R casts exactly once per timed fight (model constraint, documented)'.
independent_computation.step_3_all_four_slots_are_ready_at_t0: From data/champions.json, Syndra's sourced cooldowns are Q 'Dark Sphere' 7/7/7/7/7 s, W 'Force of Will' 12/11/10/9/8 s, E 'Scatter the Weak' 15/15/15/15/15 s, R 'Unleashed Power' 120/100/80 s; cast times are Q none, W none, E 0.25 s, R 0.25 s. Every slot is off cooldown at fight start, so no cooldown gate can reorder the opening. Under the mutual-exclusion rule the first casts merely serialize (t = 0, 0, 0, +0.25, +0.25...), all inside the first ~0.5 s of the 60 s window.
independent_computation.step_4_consequence: Because nothing is cooldown-gated at t=0, cast_timeline[0..3] is a verbatim echo of the configured cast order. Therefore cast_timeline[3]/slot == the 4th entry of the order the scenario configures. It is an input echo, not a derived physical quantity: no cooldown arithmetic can put E 4th unless E is 4th in the order.
independent_computation.step_5_ruling_out_E_as_a_recast: E cannot reach index 3 as a *recast*. Its cooldown is 15 s at every rank (the longest of the three basics) and it would have been cast at most ~0.5 s earlier; the first ability to come back up is always Q (7 s, or 4.375 s at 60 haste) or W (8-12 s base). So 'E at index 3' is only reachable as a first cast in 4th position.
independent_computation.step_6_what_the_old_value_means: data/worklists/f2-task.md states the engine's fallback: 'src/calculator/damage.py computes a rotation from a DEFAULT_CAST_ORDER (fixed Q,W,E,R)'. The 4th entry of that default order is exactly R — the old value. So the old timeline reproduced the naive default order in a scenario whose whole identity is a *custom* order; i.e. at position 4 the custom order was not being honoured.
independent_computation.step_7_what_the_new_value_means: E at index 3 means the resolved order's 4th entry is E, i.e. an order of the form [_,_,_,E] — a non-default order. This repo's own audit evidence attests that explicit 4-letter custom orders of exactly this shape are a real supported input: data/champion-audit/batch-p1-3.json records for Vladimir 'Q 176/W 330/R 385 with cast_order R,Q,W,E'. The order R,Q,W,E has E as its 4th entry — precisely the new value's shape.
independent_computation.step_8_domain_cross_check: Nothing in Syndra's cached wiki text forbids E being cast 4th, and nothing requires R to be 4th. R 'Unleashed Power' has no resource or sphere prerequisite ('Syndra conjures 3 Dark Spheres and additionally grabs up to 4 nearby live ones'), so R is legally castable at any position; conversely R is the one ability whose value *rises* the later it is cast relative to sphere generation, so pinning R to the 4th cast is not a rule the game imposes. The 60 s window is far shorter than R's 80-120 s cooldown, consistent with the documented 'R casts exactly once per timed fight' either way — the R/E swap at index 3 is an ordering change, not a cast-count change.
independent_computation.conclusion: cast_timeline[3]/slot = the 4th element of the scenario's configured custom cast order. The old value R is bit-for-bit the DEFAULT_CAST_ORDER (Q,W,E,R) 4th slot, which is the value a custom-order scenario shows when the custom order is being ignored; the new value E is the value it shows when a non-default order is honoured. New value is correct.

caveat: cast_timeline[3]/slot is an echo of a scenario input (the configured custom cast order), and the scenario definition lives in scripts//tests/, which this runbook forbids reading. The verdict therefore rests on: (a) the proof that index 3 must equal the 4th element of the configured order, (b) the old value being bit-identical to the documented DEFAULT_CAST_ORDER's 4th slot in a scenario named 'custom_order', and (c) an in-tree attestation that non-default orders of the form R,Q,W,E (4th entry E) are a real supported input. It would be falsified only if the scenario's declared custom order genuinely ends in R at position 4, in which case the pre-change timeline coincided with the default by accident.
